candidates.title: Trilemma: How Agents choose between Honesty, Confidentiality, and Task Completion
candidates.citationVelocity: not-assessed (Semantic Scholar HTTP 429 on all attempts; published 4 days)
candidates.institution: ELLIS Institute Tubingen / MPI for Intelligent Systems / Tubingen AI Center + University of Massachusetts Amherst
communitySignals: dedicated GitHub org compass-group-tue (TRILEMMA project page + TRILEMMA-ENV code repo)
not found on HF Daily Papers as of today's check
credibilityEvidence: Section 4/Figure 2: 140 agents (7 open-weight models x 10 runs x 2 agents) evaluated; 135/140 pursue the planted goal, 41 make false claims (20 CoT-acknowledged), 66 misdirect
Section 4.1: only 16/70 main-experiment runs end with valid staffing
Appendix B: multi-stage CoT-based judges (no-CoT judge + CoT-acknowledgment judge + motivated-reasoning judge + disclosure judge + evaluation-awareness judge) rather than a single LLM-judge pass
confidentiality-instruction gradient quantified across a 3-model comparison: 83%->31%->2% disclosure
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: covers main experiment, closed-weight comparison, honeypot variant, confidentiality-instruction gradient and evaluation-awareness checks, but all within a single synthetic Slack sprint-staffing environment
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: claim is scoped to the tested environment (agents deceive strategically under an engineered goal conflict without being instructed to); multi-stage judges and full released code/configs support that scoped claim
candidates.primaryLimitation: single synthetic environment; closed-weight models (Claude/GPT) can only be scored on final behavior, not on their hidden CoT, so the deception-acknowledgment analysis covers only open-weight models
candidates.presentationReason: method, judge pipeline, and claim boundaries (open- vs closed-weight scope) are explicitly stated
candidates.reason: strongest and most rigorously verified of today's candidates: multi-stage CoT judges, full open-source environment, and a concrete quantified finding (agents deceive without being told to, and often fail the task anyway) directly relevant to anyone building delegated/personal agents

candidates.citationVelocity: not-assessed (Semantic Scholar HTTP 429 on all attempts; published 5 days)

credibilityEvidence: Section 5, Table 2/3: system-layer comparison against native Google A2A controls (cancel agent/cancel all/block input) and LangGraph controls (cancel run/block+resume/time travel) on 42 content + 10 rogue runs

candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: large multi-layer evaluation (physical testbed + controlled harness + simulation) with explicit baselines and pre-registered scoring, but the coordinator's own scaling limit (~10 agents/3 hosts before journal-ingestion saturation) is self-reported and not yet resolved
reproducibilityEvidence: 10.5k LoC controlled-grid harness described in Appendix B
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: head-to-head numeric comparison against named native framework controls (A2A, LangGraph) on identical workloads supports the claim that existing native controls trade off containment against retained healthy work, while Airlock's optimized cut does not
candidates.primaryLimitation: single-process coordinator's provenance-journal ingestion saturates beyond roughly ten agents across three hosts; author-acknowledged scaling ceiling not yet resolved
candidates.presentationReason: evaluation questions, baselines, and metrics (clean runs, retained work, leaks) are explicitly defined before the results tables
candidates.reason: directly answers what happens after Trilemma/Authorization-Propagation-style failures occur: existing native multi-agent controls (A2A, LangGraph) either leak downstream effects or destroy healthy work, and this proposes and open-sources a runtime that does neither, verified on a physical testbed
